sources.title: White House Weighs Folding FDIC Into Other Agencies
OCC combines supervision into single unit

status_summary: No bill or order merging these regulators was found. A report dated 2025-02-12, citing the Wall Street Journal, described the White House as weighing folding the FDIC into Treasury or combining its supervisory role with the OCC, without any decision. The OCC announced on 2025-04-16 that it would combine its large, midsize and community bank supervision units into one division effective 2025-06-02, which is an internal reorganization, not a merger of agencies.
title: Merge the bank and credit union regulators into one supervisor
uncertainties: Reported consideration of a plan is not treated as an event, and the OCC internal reorganization is not an agency merger, so the timeline is empty. Two web searches by the researcher and one in review found no merger bill; Congress records were not searched directly. Checked systematically on 2026-10-18: Federal Register searches for the four regulators, the agenda and proposed-rule listings, a congress.gov and govinfo.gov bill search, available agency newsrooms and a news search found no bill, order or law merging the OCC, FDIC, NCUA and the Board's supervisory functions. The FDIC and OCC newsrooms could not be read and the agenda listings were not directly readable, so absence is established from the other checks.
